title: Vardanank
author: Derenik Demirchyan
short_summary: Vardanank is a historical novel set in 5th-century Armenia, when the Sassanid Persian Empire tries to force the Christian Armenian people to abandon their faith. It follows Vardan Mamikonian, the general chosen to lead Armenia's resistance, as nobles, priests, and ordinary villagers must decide how far they will go to defend what they believe in. The story builds toward the Battle of Avarayr in 451 AD, a clash remembered ever since as a defining stand for Armenian identity.
extended_summary:
In the 5th century, the powerful Sassanid Persian Empire ruled over Armenia and pressured its people to give up Christianity for the Persian state religion of Zoroastrianism. Derenik Demirchyan's novel Vardanank brings this turning point to life, showing how Armenian nobles, clergy, and common people argued, doubted, and ultimately united behind Vardan Mamikonian, a skilled and thoughtful military leader, to resist losing their faith and their way of life.

The novel builds toward the Battle of Avarayr in 451 AD, where Vardan's outnumbered Armenian forces faced the much larger Persian army. Though Vardan himself died in the battle and the Armenians did not win outright on the battlefield that day, their fierce resistance made such an impression that Persia eventually allowed Armenians to keep practicing Christianity. Because of this, Avarayr and Vardan Mamikonian are remembered not as a defeat but as one of the most important moments in Armenian history — a story about standing firm for one's beliefs even when the odds are against you.
